name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,117

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the kitchen tool

blocks.note: a grater shreds cheese; said out loud it matches a comparative adjective

explanation.surface: Someone praising a superior gadget they have heard about for the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater is the comparative of great, describing something bigger, grander or more remarkable.

blocks.note: a general is a senior army officer
a staff is a stick you lean on for support

explanation.surface: Backing given to the people who draw up battle plans.
explanation.definitionFit: The general staff is the group of officers who assist a commander with strategy and planning in an army.

clue.text: Maths statement mangled in a quote

indicators.note: something mangled has been crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all eight letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: A mathematical claim has been garbled when cited by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An equation is a formula asserting that two expressions are equal, a basic statement in mathematics.

indicators.note: the middle of a word means its central letters only are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the two central letters of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted towards the centre of a region.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to rush or dash at speed, and its past tense matches the past tense of the clue's verb.

clue.text: Romance on vacation overdue to recount

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its inside letters, leaving the two ends

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
something overdue has arrived late

explanation.surface: A holiday love affair that is long past is retold afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' reads as a holiday fling, but it empties the word of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it, so recount and relate are synonyms.

clue.text: Cow at this place to wade across

blocks.note: here means in this place
to ford a river is to wade across it at a shallow point

explanation.surface: A cow wading through a stream at this very spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford is a breed of red-and-white beef cattle, named after the English county, so one animal is an example.

blocks.note: a tax is a load or strain one carries, as in taxing work
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loaded with luggage takes a rented car.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a car with a driver that passengers pay to ride in for a single journey.

clue.text: Fashionable poem not finished by social creature

indicators.note: a word not finished is missing its final letter

blocks.note: an elegy is a mournful poem
ants live in organised colonies, the classic social insect

explanation.surface: A stylish poem left incomplete by some sociable person.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means stylish and graceful in dress or manner, much as fashionable people are.

clue.text: Lastly, have me roam around Oxford area

indicators.note: letters that roam around wander out of their places into a new order

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: Someone finally allowed to wander about the city of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lastly' looks like an instruction to take a final letter, but the whole word is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames Valley is the region of southern England along the river Thames, with Oxford as one of its main cities.

indicators.note: something reshaped is given a new form, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A Scottish lake reformed by natural forces, which do not care.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neutral means taking no side and having no preference, which is to be unconcerned either way.

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A nation described as a terrible zone of lawbreaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is a federal republic, commonly called by the continental name of its land.

clue.text: Top of bill, turned over, gives information

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the star is the headline act at the top of a theatre bill

explanation.surface: A headline performer, flipping through the programme, passes on details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of bill' looks like an instruction to take the first letter, but it means the headline act.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is slang for informing on someone to the authorities, so it rats means it squeals or tells tales.

blocks.note: the definite article singles out a particular one
a louvre is a slatted window shutter

explanation.surface: A fussy choice of window shutter for a gallery building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre in Paris is one of the world's most famous art museums, home of the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Item under shirt is cause of baby’s discomfort

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one part under another places it later in the word

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
an item is a thing

explanation.surface: Something worn under an infant's top is making the baby uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Teething is the cutting of a baby's first teeth through the gums, which is notoriously painful.

indicators.note: something manufactured is made from raw materials, so the letters are built into a new order

blocks.note: all eight letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: A wicked gang has made a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile describes a substance or temper liable to blow up or change suddenly and violently.

clue.text: A few words by daughter given judge’s decision

blocks.note: a sentence is a short group of words
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter's brief remarks were followed by a court ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A convicted person who has received a court's punishment ruling has been sentenced.

blocks.note: first meaning: a covering laid over a floor
second meaning: to call someone in and scold them

explanation.surface: Someone knocked flat by a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floored' suggests a person knocked down; here it means something put on the floor. 'Carpet' as a verb for scolding is chiefly British.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug spread across a room covers the floor, and being called on the mat or rug means being scolded by a superior.

clue.text: It's very hot coming down the slopes

definitions.text: It's very hot coming down the slopes

blocks.clueFragment: It's very hot coming down the slopes
blocks.note: surface reading: a skier or a trendy run on the ski slopes

blocks.clueFragment: It's very hot coming down the slopes
blocks.note: setter's reading: molten rock flowing down a volcano's sides

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' and 'slopes' suggest a fashionable ski resort, but the slopes belong to a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock erupting from a volcano is extremely hot and runs downhill along its flanks.

clue.text: One more answer by different woman?

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer
a different woman is not her, read as one run of letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled solver wonders whether another lady supplied the reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split of the answer into two everyday words.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one of the same kind, exactly one extra.

indicators.note: not tells us to leave something out of the word before it

blocks.note: gowns are long dresses for formal occasions
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone possesses evening wear that is not very impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, so the singular verb matches its partner.

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of, so the letters lie inside the next word

blocks.note: letters two to five of the word

explanation.surface: An unpredictable element of a musical stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song for one voice, a standard set piece in operas.

blocks.note: first meaning: favouring one side
second meaning: incomplete, covering only part

explanation.surface: Favouritism shown towards certain people.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means both prejudiced in favour of a side and existing only in part rather than whole.

clue.text: One engaged to secure new funding

blocks.note: a fiancé is a man engaged to be married
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A betrothed person trying to obtain fresh money.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance means money or funds provided for a project, so it is a synonym of funding.
